correctness.rationale: The group commutator is the alternating unimodular R-form ω. For arbitrary subgroup H, orthogonality to W=πH is equivalent to orthogonality to its R-span U=RW, so C_G(H)=π⁻¹(U^⊥). The coefficient-of-t^(ℓ−1) additive character gives a nondegenerate bicharacter; for R-submodules U its character-annihilator equals the R-annihilator, hence |U||U^⊥|=|R|^(2n) and U^⊥⊥=U even for nonfree U. Combining centralizer size and |H|=|H∩Z||W| proves the displayed exact measure and equality iff Z⊆H and W R-stable. Orthogonal duality then identifies every centralizer with an optimal-measure subgroup. For any ring |R|>p, the span of a nonzero vector by F_p yields a strict drop above Z; for R=F_p every additive W is R-linear and the measure is monotone. Independent full RREF linear-subspace enumeration confirmed [67 additive,15 R-stable] over F₂[t]/t² and [212,23] over F₃[t]/t²; these examples corroborate but do not establish the all-rank theorem.
